evidence.observation: D3 proposes that included elements skip U2–U6 and U8. The risk table says, "An unattended host writes its own \"reviewed\" include and so carries `confirmed` claims into an unattended model" and "GND cannot know who wrote a file". Standalone include validation checks validity, not owner review; attribution counts and a pin do not establish review.

concerns.recommendation: Define and verify an owner-controlled trust binding for exempt includes, or narrow the goal and documentation to explicitly trusted, owner-supplied files.
concerns.title: An unattended host can launder unreviewed confirmed claims through an include

evidence.observation: D4 admits no documents "while the root owns no object type, fact type or constraint", but the risk control claims "U1 stays whenever the root owns an element". Operations and their obligations are root-owned provenance-bearing claims; current U2 examines them, while U4, U5 and the span walk do not require their spans. The stated predicate therefore admits a root with such claims and no source document.

concerns.recommendation: Make the document-free exception require a genuinely empty authored claim surface, including operations and obligations, and test that boundary.
concerns.title: The U1 exception permits owned claims before a source document exists

evidence.observation: VG3 promises, "Every included element is reported with its include." D5 instead specifies "one line per include" containing counts, and VG3-C6 checks only those lines. When validation has no diagnostic for an element, the proposed output does not identify that element's include.

concerns.recommendation: Add an element-to-include attribution output and criterion, or revise the completion predicate to promise only per-include summaries and diagnostic attribution.
concerns.title: VG3’s reporting criterion does not demonstrate its per-element claim

evidence.observation: VG1-C2–C5 require "under 10 s in process", a wall-time doubling ratio, and "under 20 s" without specifying reference hardware or load. The plan acknowledges a "flaky" time-bound test on a loaded machine. The draft VG1 spec, line 198, uses the minimum of three runs for the ratio, which still depends on runner speed and contention.

concerns.recommendation: Specify a reproducible performance environment for the absolute bounds and make a machine-independent work or call-count invariant the required regression gate.
concerns.title: VG1 acceptance depends on the machine running the tests

summary: The plan needs a trustworthy boundary for reviewed includes, a tighter first-document rule, and criteria that match its attribution and performance claims.
